title: session-migration-proto-cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference / brain dump for a lightweight session-migration protocol for client<>edge<>server flows. Goal is to allow in-flight conversations to be moved between endpoints (client reconnect, edge failover, private deployment handoff) with minimal token re-synthesis and strong anti-replay properties. This is a personal design sketch, not a finished API.

Goals and constraints:
- Minimize re-generation: allow receiver to resume using existing KV cache / latest prefix when possible.
- Secure and auditable: migrations must be authenticated and auditable; short-lived proofs preferred.
- Incremental and composable: support partial snapshots + patches instead of shipping whole history.
- Graceful fallback: if migration fails, client retries to original or alternative endpoint without user-visible duplication.
- Keep binary sizes small for mobile edge transfers; prefer compact binary blobs (but model for JSON-first for now).

High-level flow (sequence):
1) Client opens session with primary endpoint (A).
2) Client receives session_id, kv_summary (compact), and a session_version token.
3) Primary periodically emits lightweight checkpoint deltas to client (or client can request).
4) On reconnect or failover, client requests a transfer token from primary OR requests transfer via control-plane (depending on trust domain).
5) Client presents transfer token to target endpoint (B). Endpoint B uses token to: verify, pull snapshot from primary (or from cloud store), and attempt fast-attach using KV prefix.
6) Endpoint B responds with attach_result: success (attached, resume_seq) or degrade (must rehydrate N previous tokens), or full re-sync required.
7) Client switches to B and continues.

Minimal API shapes (HTTP/JSON for readability). These are intentionally compact but expressive enough to implement in the proxy/edge.

POST /session/create
Request body:
{
  "client_id": "string",
  "initial_system_prompt": "string",
  "client_features": ["compact-checkpoints","delta-push"]
}
Response body:
{
  "session_id": "sid_...",
  "session_version": "v1",
  "kv_summary": "base64-or-compact-json",
  "transfer_policy": "attach-only | allow-remote-pull",
  "expires_at": "ISO-8601"
}

POST /session/{session_id}/checkpoint
(used by primary to push or client to pull)
Request body (push):
{
  "checkpoint_id": "chk_...",
  "base_version": "v1",
  "delta_blob": "base64",             // compact delta of KV / prefix tokens
  "sequence": 124,
  "signed_by": "edge-a",
  "ttl_seconds": 3600
}
Response:
{ "ack": true, "stored_at": "ISO-8601" }

POST /session/{session_id}/request-transfer
(Request initiated by client when wanting to move)
Request body:
{
  "target_host": "edge-b.redwood.example",
  "requested_mode": "hot-attach | cold-pull | transfer-only",
  "proof_of_possession": "jwt-or-sig",
  "client_last_seq": 124
}
Response body (from primary):
{
  "transfer_token": "tt_...",
  "allowed_until": "ISO-8601",
  "attach_hint": "kv_summary_ref://s3/path-or-blob-id",
  "required_min_seq": 120
}

POST /session/{session_id}/attach
(issued to target endpoint with transfer_token)
Request body:
{
  "transfer_token": "tt_...",
  "client_assertion": "jwt_signed_by_client",
  "client_last_seq": 124,
  "capabilities": ["resume-kv","prefix-cache" ]
}
Response body (target endpoint):
{
  "attach_result": "attached | degrade | require_full",
  "resume_seq": 124,
  "rehydrate_from": "blob://... (optional)",
  "estimated_rehydration_time_ms": 60
}

Checkpoint / snapshot format (informal):
- header: { version, checkpoint_id, base_version, seq_start, seq_end, node_id }
- index: small map of keys -> (offset, length) for fast lookup
- data: concatenated compact token blocks or token-ids + hashes
- signature: node-sig over header+index (ed25519)

Security model notes:
- Transfer token is short-lived (~1–5 minutes) and single-use.
- Tokens are issued by the primary only after it verifies client possession (client assertion).
- Target endpoint must validate token signature and optionally call back to control-plane for revocation check.
- All checkpoint blobs signed by origin node; endpoints verify signature when attaching.
- Optional HSM/KMS envelope for private deployments.

Conflict handling / concurrent attaches:
- If multiple attaches happen, primary picks winner by highest sequence or tie-breaker (node priority list).
- Targets must accept 'degrade' result: resume with N tokens re-sent to rebuild short context.
- Clients must detect duplicate echoes and deduplicate locally by server-assigned message ids.

Edge cases and heuristics:
- Unavailable primary but checkpoint store reachable: target can pull latest checkpoint directly from store if transfer_token includes read grant.
- Offline client resume: client can upload its own locally cached delta to help attach (client-sent patch).
- Large contexts: if delta size > X KB, prefer streaming rehydration (range requests) rather than single blob.
- Partial attach: if only prefix cached, attach_result="degrade" with info about how many tokens to re-send from client.

Operational signals to emit (for Console dashboards):
- transfer_requested, transfer_completed, attach_success, attach_degrade, rehydrate_time_ms, aborted_transfer, revoked_token_used

Monitoring + SLAs:
- Target attach latency 50–200ms for hot-attach; rehydrate SLA depends on blob size (p50 < 200ms for <= 16KB).
- Emit traces across client->primary->target for correlation id (session_id + transfer_id).

Open questions / TODOs (quick list):
- Token format: JWT vs compact binary signed token? Which has smaller mobile footprint?
- How to handle cross-tenant transfers in multi-tenant private deployments? (likely disallow or require explicit org-level grant)
- Compact on-wire representation: prefer CBOR/MessagePack for mobile; need a spec for a v1 binary checkpoint.
- What level of audit logging required for compliance customers? (store snapshots? store manifests only?)
- Race between primary expiring token and target trying to pull: add a short grace window in primary or have control-plane escrow.

Implementation notes (practical):
- Start with JSON-over-HTTPS endpoints; later add compact binary + gRPC for high-performance edges.
- Reuse existing KV-checkpoint blob store (s3-style) and sign with node keys (ed25519).
- Add TransferService to control-plane that can broker tokens for cross-region transfers.

Testing checklist:
- unit tests: token expiry, single-use enforcement, signature verification, attach-degrade path
- integration: client reconnect sim, target cold-pull from store, concurrent attach stress test
- e2e: mobile reconnections on flaky networks with partial uploads

Notes to self:
- Keep minimal fields in transfer_token so it's safe to leak in logs for debugging (no full checkpoint content).
- Document expected size ranges for delta_blob and design thresholds (16KB/128KB)
- Spin up small PoC between local proxy (golang) and runtime-lite (python) to test attach latency.

References / links:
- Related ticket: JIRA:ENG-7241 (session migration spike)
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/893 (kv checkpoint prototype)
- Old brainstorming doc: confluence:Quick-Checkpoints-2019 (archaic ideas but useful)

Last thoughts:
This is intentionally pragmatic; first iteration should focus on hot-attach for short-term resumes (few hundred tokens) and a simple single-use transfer_token model. If that works reliably we can iterate on streaming rehydration and binary compression.

-- A.K.
